newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong dollar firms as handover worries fade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong dollar firms as handover worries fade.

text.p: The Hong Kong dollar firmed sharply on Monday as traders unwound positions taken to counter uncertainty associated with the territory's return to Chinese rule on July 1.
The Hong Kong dollar moved quickly from about HK$7.7415 to test the key HK$7.7400 level against the U.S. dollar, but failed to breach it.
Dealers said the move followed the relaxation of currency forwards, or swaps, and reflected improved market confidence about the sovereignty transition.
"The market expected that after July 1 people would unwind their positions taken before the handover in case anything happened," one trader said.
Currency forwards or swaps allow traders to guarantee the sale or purchase of Hong Kong dollars at a future date and an agreed-upon rate.
If there is any suggestion of future uncertainty in the spot rate, dealers move fast to pick up forward positions and ensure they will be able to meet their future business commitments.

As concern about the handover approached, currency forwards moved wider. Two weeks before the transition to Chinese rule, currency forwards moved quickly to 135 points in the three-month and 240 in the six-month.

By Monday, currency forwards had fallen back to 50 points in the three-month and 100 points in the six-month, but there is still some way to go before they move back to more usual levels of 13 and 40 respectively.

A break of HK$7.7400 was expected later on Monday as more liquid conditions allowed more traders to unwind their positions. But longer term, the unit was expected to fall back below the HK$7.7400 level again.

Dealers said they started to unwind positions almost as soon as Hong Kong's small and illiquid currency market reopened on Thursday last week, but trading volumes were so thin the spot rate remained little changed until Monday.

"First we saw the forwards come off, but trading conditions were very thin last Thursday and Friday. Now trading volumes are starting to pick up and the forwards activity is spilling over into the spot rate," the dealer said.
Generally, the market tone was stable, with the overnight rate firm at 5.37 percent - below a key barrier of 5.50 percent.
